rule: Row 0 is a legend of colours to delete. The scaffold below is split into rigid pieces. A pole (a vertical run of 2 or more cells) is one piece together with any foot leaving its bottom cell. Every other horizontal run, including a pole's top bar, is its own piece. A pole whose tip sits on a free beam of another colour gets one hidden extension cell inside that beam. Legend-colour pieces are removed. Then every unsupported piece drops one row at a time, all together, until all pieces are supported. Support comes from the floor, from resting on or overlapping a supported piece, or from a horizontal run wedged between supported cells at both ends. If no legend colour is present, the output equals the input.
scope: Delete legend-coloured scaffold pieces, then settle rigid poles/feet and separate bars under floor, contact, overlap and two-sided wedging support. Preserve the canonical hidden pole-tip extension under free beams.

authored_scope: Random scenes are banded scaffolds. They contain poles on the floor, on decks, or on the feet of hanging Ls; flush, short and tall poles; decks made of free beams, top bars or wedged-L slots; feet; and optional planks. Colours are assigned so that same-colour objects never touch, even diagonally. The answer is computed only from latent pieces with the generator's own gravity simulation. Supported controls: width and height (9..30 each, either one alone or both); an explicit legend of 1..9 distinct colours; mode in identity, delete, motion, reveal or foot; and explicit latent scaffolds (3..30), which validate() uses to rebuild every canonical pair exactly. Tall grids are steered to cover at least 45% of the vertical span. Band heights grow up to 8 and band counts grow with height. Deliberately not supported: diagonal or non-stick shapes, structures touching column 0, column width-1 or row 1, legends placed anywhere other than row 0 starting at x=0, and backgrounds other than 0.
authored_constraints: Background 0 is the strict plurality colour: scaffold ink plus legend is less than half the grid.
Objects in random scenes never overlap, and same-colour objects are never 8-adjacent. The grid parse into poles, feet, top bars and free beams therefore equals the latent pieces.
Every scaffold is stable before deletion under the floor, contact, overlap and wedge support rules.
A post with both a top bar and a foot never has a 2-cell pole, so no extra vertical run can form.
Legend colours are distinct integers 1..9, and duplicates are rejected. A random scene always keeps at least one colour outside the legend.
Every mode except identity requires at least one legend colour to be present and at least one piece to survive.
Reveal mode requires a deleted free beam under a kept pole of another colour, plus movement. Foot mode requires a pole-with-foot piece to move. Delete mode requires no movement.
Explicit scaffolds are bounds-checked before cells are expanded. Malformed widths, heights, legends, modes and objects raise ValueError.
All retry loops are bounded: at most 600 geometries with 6 colourings each, and settling is bounded by height times piece count.
